title: Why Loops Exist
summary: Discover why typing the same thing over and over is a problem — and how loops fix it.

content.title: The Copy-Paste Problem
content.summary: Repeating `print()` over and over is slow. There has to be a better way.
content.body: Imagine you want a robot to shout `"Jump!"` five times. You could write this:
content.note: That works. But what if you want it 100 times? Or 1000? There has to be a better way.

content.title: Loops to the Rescue
content.summary: A `for` loop tells Python to repeat a block of code a set number of times.
content.body: Python has a trick called a **for loop**. It lets you say "do this X times" in just two lines:
content.note: That does the exact same thing as writing `print("Jump!")` five times — Python just handles the repetition for you.

content.title: What Does Each Part Mean?
content.summary: `for` starts the loop, `range(5)` controls how many times, and the indented line is what runs each time.
content.body: Let's break down a `for` loop, piece by piece:
content.note:
• `for` — starts the loop
• `i` — a counter variable Python updates automatically
• `range(5)` — tells Python to repeat 5 times
• The indented line — the code that runs each time

The indented block is called the **loop body**. Every time Python counts, it runs that block.

content.title: Indentation Is the Rule
content.summary: The loop body must be indented 4 spaces. Code outside the loop runs once after the loop finishes.
content.body: The loop body must be **indented** — moved in by 4 spaces.
content.note: If you forget the indent, Python shows an `IndentationError`.

content.title: How many times will this run?
content.summary: The number inside `range()` is how many times the loop repeats.
content.body:
How many times will this code print `"Hi!"`?

```
for i in range(4):
    print("Hi!")
```

puzzle.explanation: `range(4)` tells the loop to repeat **4 times**. The indented `print` runs once for every step.

steps.instruction: Step 1: Replace the three `print("Charge!")` lines with a `for` loop that prints `"Charge!"` 3 times. Remember: the line inside the loop must be indented (4 spaces).
steps.starterCode:
